speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what are the main reasons for many healthier foods to be more expensive than unhealthy foods despite healthier foods requiring less processing than unhealthy foods; and (b) whether there will be public education campaigns to (i) help people understand and manage their calorie intake, (ii) increase public awareness of lower sugar choices in the food types commonly consumed by Singaporeans and the problems of artificial sweeteners and (iii) educate consumers on how to eat healthier without incurring higher food bills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Ingredients and food products labelled with the HCS logo − this is the red pyramid − have been well-received by consumers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: There are currently about 3,500 food products with the HCS logo, spanning 70 food and drinks categories.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: There are ways to eat healthily without buying expensive food.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: For example, we can eat in moderation and we can choose foods with less oil and salt, or drinks with less sugar or, even better, no sugar.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) Foodfare sells its pre-packaged drinks with the HCS logo at $0.10 cheaper to encourage more consumers to choose these healthier options.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: HPB has developed lower-cost healthier recipes which are shared with the community through partners, such as the Diabetic Society of Singapore, TOUCH Community Services and NTUC SilverACE.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Since December 2016, HDP has been extended to hawker centres and coffee shops, where lower-calorie meals are tagged with a "lower in calories" label.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: HPB has also implemented various public education initiatives, such as the calorie literacy initiative My Healthy Plate and the Eat Drink Shop Healthy Campaign, to reward consumers when they choose healthier options.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This complements our healthy meals programme in schools which promotes the drinking of plain water.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: There is now a growing variety of healthier sugars available for product formulation, such as those derived from natural sources like beetroot.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: They do not increase blood sugar levels as much as conventional sugars like sucrose and fructose.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) is working with the F&B industry to explore the use of these natural sweeteners as part of their product innovation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We will continue our efforts to raise public awareness and foster a supportive environment for consumers to make healthier F&B choices, and to keep Singaporeans healthy and active.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Very often, we go to stores and we find items that are labelled with "low sugar content" cost more than those with "normal sugar content".

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: To the general public, they do not understand why items with low sugar, which is healthier, which they want to choose, but it costs more.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The simple thinking is that low sugar means put less sugar, so it should cost at least the same, or not much higher.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have seen items that are, for example, "normal sugar content", cost, say, $3 and the one with "low sugar" costs $4.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, if we want to encourage people to move to a healthier diet, could MOH educate the public on why there is such a big difference?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, this is one way of helping consumers to be able to have options, including healthier options, to help them to make healthier F&B choices.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But Mr Speaker, I want to go back to what I mentioned in my main reply earlier that, eating healthily, there are many different ways of doing so.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For example, it is about choosing the amount we eat, deciding on how much we want to eat, eating in moderation.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is also about how we prepare the food, such as if we steam, compared to deep fry.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If we use less oil, less salt, less sugar, less sauces, all these are steps which we can take to prepare healthier food options.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We are also working with our research institutes to look at how the food is prepared as it can also make a difference to the glycemic index.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is a way of measuring, after we have consumed the food, how quickly our blood sugar level will rise.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For food with lower glycemic index, there will be a smaller increase in the blood sugar level.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Other things that they have found include adding, for example, a little bit of chicken stock, or a small amount of healthy oil to the rice will also help to lower the glycemic index.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: How we eat the food also makes a difference.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Before we begin our meal, if we consume some proteins, for example, clear chicken stock or a glass of unsweetened soya bean milk before we eat our main meal, these will also help to lower the glycemic index of the meal.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Or eating it with vegetables, not just the rice alone, and with protein.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, there are many, many different ways that we can educate consumers and give them more information to help them to make healthier choices.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: I was referring to the same brand of kaya.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: The only difference is which one is less sugar.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: The actual price is $2.95 versus $3.95 for the one with the lower sugar content.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I do not know which brand of kaya he is referring to.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But because it is quite sweet, I try not to eat too much of it.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think that is one way of making a healthier choice, which is to consume less of it.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: When we spread the kaya on the bread, do not spread it so thickly.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That will be one way of helping to lower the amount of sugar that we consume.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, when we produce it and there are inadequate economies of scale, the merchant finds it difficult to price it at a very competitive level.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We see this happening with healthier cooking oils, with wholemeal bread.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: During the initial phase when the healthier products are being introduced, it will have to go through this phase where consumers are getting used to it, and the demand is not quite picking up during the initial phase.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, during this period, the lack of scale then leads to prices being higher on a per unit basis.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I do not know if this is the reason for the particular brand of kaya that Mr Chong spoke about, but this is a general observation that we see for different types of food products.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Given the Senior Minister of State's passion for healthy food, the least we can do is to take heed of his advice at the tea break later.
